questions: Did this eye problem start suddenly, after a specific event like a car crash or a fall?
Have you been diagnosed with diabetes?
Do you have double vision when looking straight ahead?
Is the movement of your right eye (the one on the left side of the screen) restricted in any direction?
results: 1. adduction in horizontal gaze (each eye): limited adduction of the RIGHT eye that fails to cross the midline, with abducting nystagmus of the left eye on left gaze - mimics an INO
2. MRI sella and orbits: subtle MEDIAL ORBITAL WALL FRACTURE with medial rectus involvement; no brainstem pathology
3. CT head (non-contrast): multiple skull fractures and epidural haemorrhage; NO evidence of brainstem injury
4. forced duction test: restriction consistent with a mechanical cause
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Pseudo-internuclear ophthalmoplegia secondary to medial rectus muscle entrapment from a medial orbital wall fracture

1. True Internuclear Ophthalmoplegia (INO) due to traumatic brainstem injury
2. Direct traumatic myopathy or rupture of the medial rectus muscle
3. Orbital compartment syndrome
dx: Pseudo-internuclear ophthalmoplegia secondary to medial rectus muscle entrapment from a medial orbital wall fracture
